findings.title: Ratified candidate preserves database ownership and destructive SQL semantics
findings.observation: Compared the exact candidate to unchanged lifecycle and Compose source. Startup and post-reset pg_isready target container loopback 127.0.0.1:5432. Startup probes receive the positive remaining monotonic deadline and backoff is capped by remaining time; the timeout handler raises a sanitized error without replay. Ordinary Compose startup remains byte-preserved. Namespace derivation, environment ownership, credentials/redaction, socket psql, ON_ERROR_STOP, DROP then CREATE, connection discovery and cleanup remain otherwise byte-preserved. Independently executing the candidate only in memory with a fake runner/clock produced delayed TCP readiness followed by exactly one DROP and CREATE, permanent unready and probe-timeout termination at a two-second bound with zero SQL, failed DROP with no CREATE, and failed CREATE with neither statement replayed. These review experiments validate the ratified governance candidate only, not future KL074 execution checks.
